title: Constitutional Council approves France's assisted-dying law
subhead: The legislation grants adults suffering from an incurable condition the right to assisted dying. The Council's decision is a victory for President Emmanuel Macron, who promised such a law when he was re-elected for a second term in 2022.

French taxpayers' data stolen in hack of Finance Ministry
subhead: The Finance Ministry acknowledged on Thursday that it had fallen victim to another cyberattack. The full extent of the breach remained unclear, but it could concern several hundred thousand people in France.

title: British far right's leader Farage beats Count Binface to win by-election
subhead: Reform UK leader Nigel Farage won with 63% of the vote in an election that was boycotted by the major parties. A parliamentary probe into undisclosed gifts he received was subsequently reopened.

title: Ryusuke Hamaguchi, director of 'All of a Sudden': 'I tend to create my works from dialogue'
subhead: The filmmaker drew inspiration from correspondence between a nursing home director and a theater director facing terminal cancer. True to his discreet nature, Hamaguchi refuses to have his cinema reflect his personal convictions.

title: One-person households' struggle for housing: 'It would be much easier as a couple. I feel like I'm being punished twice'
subhead: Some 12 million people live alone in France, and their number continues to rise. The country's housing stock has not kept pace with this trend, exacerbating the impact of the housing crisis on these individuals.

'I'll pay for a breast. Even both, if you want': The costs, big and small, of breast surgery in the private sector
subhead: 'My Breasts and Me' (5/5). In France, one out of every two patients chooses the private sector for breast reconstruction. Some are willing to give up their vacations, take out a loan or turn to their parents for help. Le Monde spent several weeks inside a private breast surgery practice in Paris.

title: Trump's secret exfiltration betrays nerves and improvisation over his security
subhead: Following the NATO summit on July 8 in Ankara, journalists believed they were traveling with the US president aboard the former Air Force One plane. In reality, the president had been discreetly transferred to another aircraft due to threats from Iran, the 'Washington Post' and 'New York Times' revealed.

title: Finland wants to restore its peatlands to help the environment. And to slow Russian tanks.
subhead: The Nordic country has identified 180,000 hectares of wetlands that, if restored, could benefit not only the climate and biodiversity but also national defense. While the military supports the plan, some environmentalists warn against rushing the process.
